page: Amazon Web Services c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2993.35 and small-model LLM text generation reaching 300.58 tokens per second. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks represents a performance tradeoff, registering in the bottom 25% for both read-only (39.28 GB/sec) and write (21.76 GB/sec) operations. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations consistently fall within average ranges.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6a.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is suited for batch processing, web serving, distributed analytics, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
